report.source_text: Lymph node biopsy revealed diffuse infiltration of small to medium-sized lymphocytes with rare nuclear irregularities, which distorted the nodal architecture. Giant cells with irregularly lobulated nuclei, like Reed-Sternberg cells, were scattered among the background lymphocytes (Fig. 1). Some macrophages and angiogenesis were also observed. On immunohistochemical analysis, the giant cells were positive for CD30 and CD15, and negative for CD3, CD20, PAX5, and Epstein-Barr virus-encoded RNA1 in situ hybridization (EBER-ISH). The background lymphocytes were positive for CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD25 (partially). These findings were consistent with lymphocyte-rich classic Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL).

report.source_text: Doxorubicin, bleomycin, vinblastine, and dacarbazine (ABVD) were first administered because the diagnosis was cHL. However, after one cycle of ABVD, the treatment regimen was changed to pirarubicin, cyclophosphamide, vincristine, and prednisolone (THP-COP) due to the diagnosis changing to Hodgkin-like ATLL. During the first cycle of THP-COP, the patient developed drug induced eruptions and grade 3 febrile neutropenia. Considering these side effects, he refused a second cycle of THP-COP and decided to receive low-dose oral chemotherapy (400 mg of sobuzoxane, 25 mg of etoposide, and 10 mg of prednisolone for 3 days every 2-3 weeks) in an outpatient setting.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 56-year-old man with HTLV-1 infection and history of HAM/TSP presented with right inguinal lymphadenopathy. Initial blood work showed high soluble IL-2 receptor and HTLV-1 positivity with no atypical lymphoid cells initially. Lymph node biopsy revealed features resembling lymphocyte-rich classic Hodgkin lymphoma with Reed-Sternberg-like giant cells positive for CD30 and CD15 and background T cells positive for CD3, CD4, CD5, and partial CD25. Southern blot detected di-clonal proviral HTLV-1 DNA bands in lymph node and peripheral blood, supporting ATLL. Later appearance of atypical lymphoid cells in peripheral blood and transient IL-2 receptor increase suggested systemic involvement. Initial treatment for cHL was changed to THP-COP regimen upon diagnosis revision. Clinical course noted complications and shift to low-dose oral chemotherapy.
